findings.text: The guest memory subsystem exposes initialization and teardown operations. Initialization associates the file operations with the owning module, creates a dedicated inode cache for guest memory inodes, and establishes its internal mount. Teardown releases the mount, clears the stored mount reference, waits for RCU callbacks, and destroys the inode cache. A configuration without support provides inline operations that succeed immediately on init and do nothing on exit.

Guest memory mount creation uses the dedicated filesystem definition and propagates mount errors to the caller. On success the mount is marked non-executable. If mount establishment fails after cache creation, the cache is destroyed and the error is returned. Cache allocation failure is reported as out of memory without attempting a mount.

Virtualization startup is gated by a load time flag. When the flag requests enablement at load, initialization attempts to enable virtualization and returns its result, while teardown disables virtualization. When the flag is not set, both operations succeed without action. An alternate build provides unconditional no operation variants that always succeed.

Virtualization enablement follows a reference counted state machine. The first acquirer performs architecture enablement, hotplug registration, and syscore registration. Additional acquirers only increment the count and return success. Failures unwind in reverse order, including architecture disablement and count decrement. Shutdown observation leads to busy failure with full unwind.

Enabling virtualization after shutdown initiation is treated as a hazard. The implementation checks global system state for halt, power off, and restart after registering shutdown handling, and refuses with a busy status if shutdown is underway. This ordering relies on system state being updated before the shutdown callback, which motivates use of syscore handling rather than a reboot notifier.
Architecture specific virtualization enablement defaults to doing nothing when no architecture override is present, allowing generic code to proceed to hotplug and syscore steps.

Debug initialization publishes virtual machine and virtual CPU statistics under a KVM directory in debugfs. For each descriptor in the VM and VCPU tables it creates a file named by the descriptor, with access mode derived from the descriptor and file operations selected by writability. The stored file context encodes the descriptor offset.
Statistic debugfs access depends on measurement type. Instantaneous values use read only mode 0444, while cumulative and peak values plus any unrecognized type use mode 0644.

The device operations table supports registration and removal by numeric type. Registration validates the type against table capacity and rejects duplicates, storing the supplied operations on success. Removal clears the entry when present and otherwise leaves the table unchanged. VFIO integration registers its operations under the VFIO type at init and removes that type at exit, with no operation fallbacks when disabled.

Global KVM teardown deregisters the control device, reverses virtualization initialization, removes the debug directory recursively, releases per CPU kick masks, destroys the VCPU cache, and then shuts down guest memory, VFIO operations, async page fault handling, and irqfd handling. SVM module exit performs this global teardown before its own SVM specific teardown.

Secure encrypted virtualization state records lifecycle flags named active, es_active and need_init, identity values asid, handle, fd and policy, resource tracking through pages_locked, regions_list and misc_cg, launch data via ap_jump_table, vmsa_features and ghcb_version, mirroring links enc_context_owner with mirror_vms and mirror_entry plus migration_in_progress, and SNP support using snp_context, guest_req_buf, guest_resp_buf guarded by guest_req_mutex, have_run_cpus and snp_certs_enabled.

SVM VM state embeds the generic VM object first, then AVIC virtualization data with VM identifier avic_vm_id plus tables avic_logical_id_table and avic_physical_id_table and hash node hnode, and optionally encrypted state sev_info when AMD SEV support is compiled in.

A VMCB reference maintains ptr with pa and cpu plus asid_generation. Per CPU data maintains asid_generation with max_asid, next_asid and min_asid, control flags flush_all_asids and bp_spec_reduce_set, save state via save_area and save_area_pa, and SEV table sev_vmcbs indexed by SEV identifier.

Cached save area retains segment state es, cs, ss and ds with gdtr and idtr plus privilege level cpl, control state efer with cr4, cr3 and cr0, debug state dr7 and dr6 with rflags, execution position rip with rsp and rax plus cr2, CET state s_cet with ssp and isst_addr, and paging plus branch tracing via g_pat, dbgctl, br_from, br_to, last_excp_from and last_excp_to.

Cached control area stores intercept bitmap intercepts with pause filtering pause_filter_thresh and pause_filter_count, permission bases iopm_base_pa and msrpm_base_pa with tsc_offset, address management asid with tlb_ctl and erap_ctl, interrupt state int_ctl, int_vector and int_state, exit reporting exit_code with exit_info_1 and exit_info_2 plus exit_int_info and exit_int_info_err, miscellaneous controls misc_ctl and misc_ctl2 with event injection event_inj and event_inj_err, execution continuation next_rip with nested_cr3, cleanliness clean, and a trailing union holding either HyperV enlightenments or reserved software bytes.

Nested state nests a second level VMCB reference vmcb02 with host save and control MSRs hsave_msr and vm_cr_msr, guest addresses vmcb12_gpa with last_vmcb12_gpa and last_bus_lock_rip, merged permission map msrpm, cached guest control ctl and save snapshot save, plus flags initialized and force_msr_bitmap_recalc for lifecycle and bitmap rebuild coordination.

Encrypted state per VCPU keeps save area vmsa with ghcb pointer, validity bitmap valid_bitmap, mapping ghcb_map and startup flags received_first_sipi with ap_reset_hold_type, scratch handling via sw_scratch with ghcb_sa, ghcb_sa_len, ghcb_sa_sync and ghcb_sa_free, page state batch progress psc using cur_idx, end_idx, batch_size and is_2m, registered address ghcb_registered_gpa, and SNP update coordination through snp_vmsa_mutex with snp_pending_vmsa_gpa, snp_guest_vmsa_gpa, snp_ap_waiting_for_reset and snp_has_guest_vmsa.

SVM VCPU state embeds the generic VCPU, VMCB shorthand vmcb with vmcb01 and current_vmcb plus asid, entry helpers sysenter_esp_hi, sysenter_eip_hi and tsc_aux, control MSRs msr_decfg, spec_ctrl, tsc_ratio_msr and virt_spec_ctrl with msrpm and next_rip, nested state, NMI handling via nmi_iret_rip, nmi_masked, awaiting_iret_completion, nmi_singlestep and related flags, software interrupt injection tracking, APIC shadow ldr_reg, dfr_reg and avic_physical_id_entry, posted interrupt list ir_list with its lock, encrypted state sev_es, and runtime flags for loaded state, AVIC window, MSR interception and guest GIF.

Virtualization reference counting is serialized by a mutex held across the whole enable sequence. Guest request bounce buffers require holding their dedicated mutex. Mirror list fields are protected by a separate SEV mirror lock. Posted interrupt lists use a per VCPU raw spinlock, and concurrent SNP save area updates use a per VCPU mutex.
Permission map sizes correspond to three pages for IO and two pages for MSRs.

VMCB cleanliness tracking assigns indices zero through twelve in listed order to intercept, permission map, address identifier, interrupt, nested paging, control registers, debug registers, descriptor tables, segments, second control register, branch records, virtual interrupt controller and CET groups, with software use fixed at thirty one. The all clean mask is the union of those bits, while the always dirty mask contains only interrupt and second control register bits.

MSR permission bitmap geometry uses two thousand forty eight bytes per range with two bits per register, yielding four registers per byte and the product as registers per range. The offset mask equals registers per range minus one.

Nested exit handling uses zero for host handled, one for nested exit completed, and two for needing further checks. AVIC operation requires absence of thirteen inhibit conditions covering disabled, absent, HyperV, nested, interrupt window, PIT reinjection, blocked interrupt, SEV, identifier aliasing and size, and APIC identifier and base modification.

Debug control reserved bits are the complement of the branch record bit. Lazy register loading covers only the page directory pointer register. The SEV fallback reports zero maximum identifiers and a not present error for attribute queries. Port IO directions are zero for input and one for output, while virtualization instruction sets are one for VMX and two for SVM.

Clearing a nested control intercept delegates to a generic bit clear on the intercept array. Extended APIC permission offset detection scales the offset by sixteen and tests membership in a two hundred fifty six entry window from the APIC base. MSR bitmap helpers compute a bit index, report success without action when unmapped, and otherwise apply the requested bit operation at read or write positions. GHCB helpers provide checked reads of save fields gated by a validity bitmap.

Enabling second level flush on HyperV obtains the partition assist page and fails with out of memory when invalid. On success it stores the page and VM identifier in the enlightenment area and sets the nested flush hypercall control once, marking the control dirty only on transition.

Instruction pointer tracing returns zero when guest state is protected and otherwise reads the guest pointer. Exit events record reason, guest pointer, instruction set, two info words, interrupt info, error code, VCPU identifier and pending requests, dispatching reason formatting by instruction set with extra flag handling for VMX. Symbol tables map delivery modes, APIC registers, exception vectors and destination shorthands to readable names.

SVM and trace headers use conventional include guards to prevent double inclusion, the trace subsystem identifies itself under the KVM name, and SVM on HyperV messages are prefixed with the module name.
